newsitem.title: USA: USDA-'96-97 world sugar output at 121.4 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: USDA-'96-97 world sugar output at 121.4 mln tonnes.

text.p: World surgar production in 1996-97 should be 121.4 million tonnes and world sugar consumption -- not adjusted for unrecorded trade -- should be 119.5 million, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.
An apparent surplus of 1.9 million tonnes disappears after adjustments for unrecorded trade, USDA said in a Situation and Outlook summary.

The world production forecast is up 1.2 million tonnes from the earlier forecast published in the June summary, and 1.5 million tonnes below the revised estimate for the global 1995-95 crop, USDA said.
Global sugar consumption for 1996-97 -- not adjusted for unrecorded trade -- was forecasted up 2.8 million tonnes from the revised estimates for the previous year, USDA said.
World sugar trade in 1996-97 was forecast at 34.9 million tonnes, or about 29 percent of forecasted production.
U.S. imports should be 2.74 million tonnes, USDA said, making the United States the second top importer and at the highest level since 1983-84.

Sugar imports are expected to remain strong in the Russian Federation at 3.2 million tonnes, while China's import were seen sliding to 2.4 million tonnes from an estimated 2.5 million the previous year.
Ending stocks for 1996-97 should be 23.4 million tonnes, slightly below last year. The forecasted stocks-to-use ratio at 19.1 percent would be down 20.3 percent from last year.
Sugar use continues to expand in Latin America, and Asia should use 42 million tonnes, up 23 percent since 1990-91.
Among the world's leading exporters, better crop prospects in Australia, Brazil, Cuba, South Africa and Thailand should allow those countries to increase exports.
India also likely will be a major exporter, but exports from Ukraine will drop to 1 million tonnes, USDA said.
The summary said raw sugar prices have been trading below the spot price and are likely to remain weak into the fall.
